interactions.summary: Jiang stops speculative answers and has a student reread Dante's lines explaining that animal and plant souls arise through mediated motion, while human life is breathed forth immediately by the chief good.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang prompt with student reading Dante

interactions.summary: Jiang uses Adam's creation to explain that humans have souls because God breathes part of himself into them, and he turns that into a model where every human action is a confused desire to return to God.

claims.claim: Jiang insists that the class should derive the answer from Dante's actual text rather than from free-floating biblical speculation.
The reread Dante passage distinguishes animal and plant souls, which are drawn from matter through holy motion, from human life, which is breathed forth immediately by the chief good.
Jiang identifies the human difference from animals and trees as the soul, grounded in the biblical scene where God breathes life into Adam.
Jiang says God put part of himself into humans, and that indwelling part is what the class calls the soul.
Jiang argues that because the soul is part of God, its deepest aspiration is always to return to God, even when humans do not consciously understand that desire.
Jiang presents the desire to return to God as a fundamental logic of the universe that underlies everything humans do.

signature_moments.moment: The packet pivots on Dante's sharp distinction between life drawn forth from matter and human life breathed forth immediately by the chief good.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your life is breathed forth immediately by the chief good
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the textual hinge Jiang uses to move from natural generation to the human soul's divine origin.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang literalizes the soul as a severed piece longing to rejoin its source.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The bodily image turns an abstract doctrine of the soul into a memorable account of metaphysical homesickness.

signature_moments.moment: Every action becomes a distorted attempt to return to God.
signature_moments.source_phrase: everything we do is because we want to return to god
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is Jiang's strongest universalization in the packet, expanding Dante's anthropology into a total motivational theory.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Dantean name in the passage for God as the immediate source of human life and soul.
The part of God breathed into humans, which gives life and drives the desire to return to its source.
Jiang's phrase for the soul's deepest aspiration and for the hidden motive beneath human action.

chronology_notes.note: After the prior packet's lawful-creation model, this packet locates the human exception in Adam's direct animation by God and expands that into a universal account of the soul's desire.
